tutorial.text: We have to do the test over and over. For this, we use the "always-if" construction.
Lawn sprouts can be separated from weeds using a vertical line.
The position of the vertical line is set by the x coordinate. The weeds are to the right of the line, hence the "greater than" sign.
You can set any number from 60 to 120 as a border. But 120 will not work because 120 is not greater than 120.

hints.text:
When you click on the How to Play button, a sprite with rules will appear. When you click on the sprite with the rules, it disappears.
When you click on the New Game button, the menu disappears and the game background and game sprites appear.
hints.title: Day 1. Create a menu with two buttons

hints.text: The cursor should change its shape when pointed at the mirror.
hints.title: Day 1. Create a script for the cursor

hints.text: The mirror should rotate when you click on it with the cursor. The glare should be in the center of the mirror and rotate with it.
hints.title: Day 1. Create a script for the glare and mirror

hints.text: Clones of the ray of light fly up and reflect off the mirror. They disappear if they touch the edge or the crystal.
hints.title: Day 1. Create a script for the rays

hints.text: The crystal brightens when a ray of light hits it. When 10 rays hit the crystal, the game ends.
hints.title: Day 2. Create a script for the crystal

hints.text: The final screen with the words "You won!" should appear at the end of the game. A second after that, a button appears on the screen to start a new game.
hints.title: Day 2. Make up the end of the game

hints.text: Often, players can return to the menu at the end of the game and start a new game from there. Redesign the project so that instead of the New Game button, the Main Menu button, which takes the player back to the menu, appears on the final screen.
